title: Some items with two right answers
statement: Include some items with more than one right answer, such as choose-two items, so learners don't come to expect exactly one right answer to every question.
example: One reading course's task bank adds a select-two item with exactly two correct answers.
detail: The task bank in a Grade 3 reading course's lesson design, whose example stems are quoted from a released Grade 3 item sampler, adds a select-two item: a multiselect with exactly two correct answers, usable on any text. It gives its reason as breaking the habit that every question has one answer.
against: It is a design decision, and no effect on learners was measured.
